u3273fa8730: ⟦1⟧Programmer USB_VCC output deviation⟦/1⟧⟦2/⟧ The programmer's USB_VCC is adjusted with a potentiometer, so the actual output voltage may deviate somewhat from the set value. The 8 channels of a programmer share one voltage reference source, so ideally all channels output the same voltage; however, because of component variations and potentiometer adjustment, the actual deviation is usually ⟦3⟧within 30mv⟦/3⟧.
u1bf72cb550: ⟦1⟧Voltage drop across the USB cable and pogo pin contact resistance⟦/1⟧⟦2/⟧ The resistance of the USB cable between the device and the programmer and the contact resistance between the fixture's pogo pins and the device's pads both cause a voltage drop. During programming, the device's current consumption is typically ⟦3⟧6–7mA⟦/3⟧; if the cable resistance and contact resistance add up to about ⟦4⟧10Ω⟦/4⟧, the voltage drop is about ⟦5⟧60mv⟦/5⟧. This is also the main reason why a device that fails programming can pass normally after the fixture is pressed down again.
ua77d499dba: ⟦1⟧USB_GND return path and sampling error⟦/1⟧⟦2/⟧ The programmer's USB_GND line includes a fixed ⟦3⟧1Ω⟦/3⟧ resistor, and the crossing of the programming wiring and the ground return paths also has some effect. The device's own sampling may deviate slightly, but this is usually negligible.

uc6ba5c6e9e: In mass production, a fixture is generally used so that N programmers program N*8 devices at the same time. While dozens of devices are being programmed simultaneously,⟦1/⟧contact problems may occur when the fixture is pressed down, some chip performance tests may be rather strict, or the chips themselves may have problems, causing programming errors on individual devices.⟦2/⟧When this happens, you may want to program only the failed devices again and avoid programming the successfully programmed devices a second time, both to avoid problems caused by repeated programming and because repeated programming may also waste the fw file's programming count, authentication codes, Bluetooth addresses and so on.
uef59e59a29: This requirement can be met by setting a board-change interval.⟦1/⟧With the board-change interval set to 1000mS, the programmer measures the time from when a successfully programmed device on the current channel goes offline (the device is removed) until programming starts again:⟦2/⟧if the interval is longer than 1000mS, all channels are allowed to program;⟦3/⟧if the interval is shorter than 1000mS, only the channels that failed are allowed to program again.
